topics.editorialRationale: Select OpenAI's customer account as a current agent deployment signal: the Amp team describes agents moving into planning, design and post-release work, with longer tasks enabled by model access and token budgets. Keep it attributed as a provider-published customer story, not independent proof of general performance.

Select the Bank of England speech for its current account of resilience amid repeated shocks. Use it as context for scenario design, not as a new supervisory requirement; connect this week's specific agent-interaction scenario to the possibility of correlated operational and financial stress.

No new third-party candidate clears the materiality and novelty bar this week. Keep shared-service failure in the editorial scenario as a control test; do not recycle GitHub status rows or the SIMEX26 exercise already discussed in prior editions.

Select the Bank of England Money Market Committee minutes as a recent primary source on market plumbing and current operating conditions. Treat meeting discussion as context for liquidity scenario design, not a change in policy or a new requirement.

The current candidate set offers no financial-crime development that changes this edition's decision test. Do not repeat the OFSI licence carried in Edition 17 or promote a general campaign notice as a new control signal.

Select the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security's 16 October advisory as a current primary vulnerability notice. Keep the response conditional on estate exposure: identify affected BeyondTrust Remote Support versions, apply the vendor fix and review indicators if present.

Select GitHub's 12 October incident as a distinct, newly dated disruption affecting Actions, pull requests and issues; it is separate from the 7 October incidents in Edition 17. Keep the claim bounded to the reported service impact and ask teams that rely on hosted delivery controls to know their release fallback.

Select the French CNIL's 16 October summary of European authorities' work on data protection and value creation in finance. It is a new cross-authority publication; describe it as practical guidance and analysis, not a new binding obligation.
